run.question:
Something's broken — we're getting paged. Look at the app-265-prod-logs index
for the last 3 hours and tell me what's going on across our fleet.

report.summary: The only multi-cluster log source available (Elasticsearch index app-265-prod-logs) contains just 7 documents in the 24h authorized window, all written between 2026-11-22T08:02:13Z and 09:32:13Z, and every ERROR-level document is from cluster production-us-east-1: payment-service logged an upstream timeout to stripe-us /v1/charges (30s) and checkout-service logged a checkout failure on the same 30s stripe-us timeout and, later, an open circuit breaker toward payment-service at a 41% failure rate. The same index shows production-eu-west-2 and production-ap-southeast-1 payment-service and checkout-service reporting healthy in INFO lines, and I directly verified in the production-eu-west-2 cluster (the only cluster my Kubernetes access covers) that the payment and checkout pods log no errors and continuously record successful payments, with all 21 otel-demo deployments at 1/1 ready. So the observed failure is confined to the production-us-east-1 payment path; the deepest point the evidence reaches is the external payment provider stripe-us, whose own state is not observable here. Metrics (Prometheus) and traces (Jaeger) were unavailable for every query in this Run, so no error-rate, latency-baseline or span evidence could be obtained and the alert that paged could not be confirmed; two fault-injection flags named paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable exist in the eu-west-2 flagd config but are off by default and eu-west-2 shows no payment errors. Side observations in production-eu-west-2: several containers terminated at 08:04:13Z (exit 255, reason Unknown) and the prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx exited on 'host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090"'; neither is tied to the payment errors by any evidence, and their cause is unknown.

claims.text: Across the whole authorized 24h window the app-265-prod-logs index holds exactly 7 documents (all 7 also fall inside the last 3h, 08:02:13Z-09:32:13Z); grouping by cluster, level and service gives ERROR buckets only for production-us-east-1 (checkout-service 2 docs, payment-service 1 doc) and INFO buckets for production-eu-west-2 and production-ap-southeast-1 (checkout-service and payment-service, 1 doc each).
payment-service in cluster production-us-east-1 logged, at 2026-11-22T09:02:13Z, level ERROR: "Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms".

checkout-service in cluster production-us-east-1 logged at 2026-11-22T08:02:13Z, level ERROR: "POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)", and at 2026-11-22T09:32:13Z, level ERROR: "Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)".

In production-eu-west-2 the index records INFO lines only: payment-service "Adyen-eu responding normally, p95 180ms" (09:32:13Z) and checkout-service "Healthy: p95 latency 218ms" (08:02:13Z); in production-ap-southeast-1 payment-service logged "All payment provider connections healthy" (09:32:13Z) and checkout-service "Healthy: success rate 99.9%" (08:02:13Z).

In the production-eu-west-2 cluster, pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d (container payment) produced 363 log lines between 07:02:21Z and 10:02:21Z and exactly one line matched the regex error|fail|timeout|stripe|circuit|unavailable: a Node (node:24) MetadataLookupWarning at 2026-11-22T08:04:24Z; no stripe, timeout or circuit-breaker lines were present.

In the same cluster, pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n produced 178 lines matching error|fail|timeout|circuit|unavailable|Payment in the window; the 80 newest shown (2026-11-22T09:02:56Z to 10:02:17Z) are all informational "payment went through (transaction_id: ...)" entries, with 98 older matching lines not shown.
All 21 otel-demo deployments in production-eu-west-2 report 1 ready and 1 available replica, including checkout (generation 1) and payment (generation 1); no deployment is short of replicas.

The otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config defines fault-injection flags with state ENABLED but defaultVariant "off": paymentFailure ("Fail payment service charge requests n%") and paymentUnreachable ("Payment service is unavailable"), plus other flags such as productCatalogFailure, cartFailure, adFailure and kafkaQueueProblems, all also defaulting to off.

The otel-demo ConfigMap prometheus contains an alerting rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (severity critical, for 2m) on checkout PlaceOrder server span error ratio > 0.5 over 5m, labeled cluster: opspilot-m1; this is rule configuration in production-eu-west-2, not evidence that the alert was firing.

The only two events in the authorized window are Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint events for Endpoints objects: "Failed to create endpoint for service app-95/orca: endpoints \"orca\" already exists" at 09:21:00Z and "Failed to create endpoint for service app-162/signup-service: endpoints \"signup-service\" already exists" at 09:32:52Z; the cluster's namespace list contains default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo, so app-95 and app-162 are not readable here.

In production-eu-west-2 several container instances last terminated at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z with exitCode 255 and reason Unknown (checkout, payment, prometheus-server, opentelemetry-collector), restartCount 2, and all those pods are Running and ready now; the prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx container has restartCount 6 with its previous instance terminated at 08:04:42Z, exitCode 1, reason Error.

The previous prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx instance logged "[emerg] host not found in upstream \"prometheus:9090\" in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:22" and "nginx: [emerg] host not found in upstream \"prometheus:9090\"" at 2026-11-22T08:04:42Z.

The Services payment and checkout exist in namespace otel-demo with selectors {opentelemetry.io/name: payment} and {opentelemetry.io/name: checkout} on port 8080 -> 8080, and their pods payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d and checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n are Running with all containers ready.

The failing dependency is the external payment provider stripe-us in the production-us-east-1 payment path: two independent services (payment-service and checkout-service) attribute 30s timeouts to stripe-us, and checkout then measured a 41% payment-service failure rate; because the provider itself is not observable from the available data, whether the stall originated at the provider or inside payment-service's own call path/dependency configuration is unverified.

The page was most likely a checkout-error-ratio alert (the only alert rule I can read is CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh on checkout PlaceOrder server error ratio > 50% for 2m, severity critical), but since Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE the firing state and the actual alert instance could not be read.

The eu-west-2 flagd fault-injection flags paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are set to defaultVariant "off", and the eu-west-2 payment pod logs contain no stripe/timeout/circuit failures while eu-west-2 checkout kept logging successful payments; nothing in the evidence shows one of these flags being enabled for the failing production-us-east-1 payment path.

The 08:04:13Z container terminations in production-eu-west-2 did not interrupt payment processing there: checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logged successful "payment went through" entries from 09:02:56Z through 10:02:17Z, and all otel-demo deployments report full ready/available replicas.

The two Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint events are not the cause of the checkout/payment failure: they concern Endpoints orca (namespace app-95) and signup-service (namespace app-162), not payment or checkout, no payment/checkout endpoint event exists, and eu-west-2 checkout continued processing payments normally around them.

The 08:04:13Z container terminations in production-eu-west-2 are not the cause of the reported errors: the first production-us-east-1 error in the index is timestamped 08:02:13Z, before that termination, the failing services are in a different cluster, and eu-west-2 payment/checkout stayed functional afterwards.

Ask the payment provider / network owners for stripe-us (/v1/charges) status and latency for production-us-east-1 during 08:02-09:32Z, and compare payment-service's provider routing and timeout configuration per region, since eu-west-2 (Adyen-eu) was reported normal at the same timestamps.

Restore the metrics and trace paths before relying on any error-rate or latency conclusion: Prometheus and Jaeger answered SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query in this Run, and in production-eu-west-2 the prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx exited on "host not found in upstream \"prometheus:9090\"", so alert rules like CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh cannot currently be evaluated from this side.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for every query in this Run (get_all_labels, get_metric_names, list_prometheus_rules, execute_prometheus_instant_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error-rate, latency or alert-firing evidence exists; the metric series traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and app_payment_transactions_total could not be read and remain unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unavailable for every query in this Run (traces_list_services, traces_search, traces_search_by_tags all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no spans, durations or parent-child call edges for payment/checkout could be verified.

Kubernetes access covers only cluster production-eu-west-2; the affected cluster production-us-east-1 (and production-ap-southeast-1) could not be inspected, so its pod status, events, restarts and application logs are unknown.

The app-265-prod-logs index contains only 7 documents, all between 2026-11-22T08:02:13Z and 09:32:13Z in the authorized 24h window, so there is no pre-incident baseline and the error onset before 08:02:13Z or recovery after 09:32:13Z is unknown.

Which alert actually paged is unknown: alert state cannot be read (Prometheus down) and no alertmanager payload is part of the evidence; the visible rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh is configuration for cluster opspilot-m1 only, and whether an equivalent rule exists for production-us-east-1 is unknown.

Whether the fault-injection flags paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable (or any other flagd flag) were switched on in production-us-east-1 at 08:02-09:32Z is unknown; only the current eu-west-2 flagd-config could be read, and it shows defaultVariant off.

The cause of the production-eu-west-2 container terminations at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z (exitCode 255, reason Unknown, across checkout, payment, prometheus-server and opentelemetry-collector) and of the prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx exit at 08:04:42Z is unknown; no pod events exist for them and the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

The two FailedToCreateEndpoint events reference namespaces app-95 (orca) and app-162 (signup-service) that are not present among the cluster's namespaces, so those objects could not be read and their relevance is unknown.
Credential values in the prometheus and otel-collector ConfigMaps are redacted, so the scrape/export auth configuration cannot be verified.
Whether stripe-us itself was degraded, and whether the 30s timeouts are provider-side or caused by payment-service's own configuration, could not be verified from the available sources.
next_steps: Obtain production-us-east-1 Kubernetes and provider monitoring access to check payment-service pod state, outbound calls to stripe-us and its provider-side latency/error rate for 08:02-09:32Z.

Restore or repair Prometheus access (prometheus-readonly-proxy upstream resolution of prometheus:9090) and Jaeger so error-rate and span evidence can confirm the checkout PlaceOrder error ratio and the payment -> stripe-us call edge.
Pull the Alertmanager notification history to identify the exact alert and label set that paged, and the time it started firing.

Confirm with the payment provider or its status page whether stripe-us /v1/charges was slow or failing during the window, and validate checkout's 30s timeout and circuit-breaker thresholds against provider p95 latency.
Review the flagd flag change history for production-us-east-1 (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable) to rule fault injection in or out.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.

content:
{"alertmanager.yml":"global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]        credentials_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]        type: Bearer
    max_alerts: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []
"}

{"relay":"connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      authenticator: basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000
"}

{"alerting_rules.yml":"groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
","alerts":"{}
","allow-snippet-annotations":"false","prometheus.yml":"global:
  evaluation_interval: 1m
  scrape_interval: 1m
  scrape_timeout: 10s
storage:
  tsdb:
    out_of_order_time_window: 30m
otlp:
    keep_identifying_resource_attributes: true
    promote_resource_attributes:
    - opspilot.integration.id
    - service.instance.id
    - service.name
